page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.32-128 is a compute-oriented virtual server based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processors. Configured with 32 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, simultaneous multithreading provides 64 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware resources for this shape are fully dedicated, eliminating CPU contention from neighboring virtual machines. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block volumes or object storage services for persistent data retention. Graphics processing units are absent from this configuration, and external network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio favors parallel processor execution over extensive memory-resident footprints. This profile provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for high-thread-count workloads where RAM demand remains modest. The architecture is matched to multi-threaded batch processing, distributed software compilation, continuous integration and build pipelines, and stateless web application serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.32-128 is a dedicated virtual machine configuration powered by Intel Xeon 8358 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at 2.6 GHz, the server delivers 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance contains no integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent state, and features no GPU acceleration hardware. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By providing dedicated vCPU allocation without burst restrictions, the server ensures deterministic processing performance. VM.Standard3.Flex.32-128 is structured for parallel compute tasks, continuous integration and build automation, multi-threaded batch workloads, and scale-out web serving tiers where compute throughput is prioritized over large RAM allocations.
